description: Implement M2 (deterministic seed + challenge codes), M3 (ghost duel), and M4 (share card)

userStories.title: Deterministic seeded pipe generation
userStories.description: Replace CGFloat.random in spawnPipePair() with a seeded PRNG so the same seed always produces the same pipe sequence. Add a seed property to GameScene that defaults to a random value for classic mode.
acceptanceCriteria: GameScene has a public `seed: UInt64` property
spawnPipePair() uses a seeded GKRandomSource (or similar) instead of CGFloat.random
Playing with the same seed produces identical pipe positions every time
Classic mode still uses a random seed each run
Build succeeds: xcodebuild -project FlapFight.xcodeproj -scheme FlapFight -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -quiet build
userStories.notes: GameScene.swift:171 is where CGFloat.random is used. Use GKMersenneTwisterRandomSource seeded with the seed value.

userStories.title: Challenge code encoder/decoder
userStories.description: Create a ChallengeCode struct that encodes a seed + target score into a short shareable string (e.g. base32/base36) and decodes it back. No UI yet, just the data layer.
acceptanceCriteria: ChallengeCode struct with `seed: UInt64` and `targetScore: Int` properties
encode() returns a short alphanumeric string (8-12 chars)
decode(code:) returns a ChallengeCode? from a string
Round-trip: decode(encode(code)) == original code
File location: FlapFight/Game/ChallengeCode.swift
Build succeeds

userStories.title: Challenge mode UI and flow
userStories.description: Add UI to enter a challenge code and play challenge mode. Show the target score during gameplay. Wire up code generation after a classic run.
acceptanceCriteria: After a classic run, the death overlay shows a challenge code for that run
RootView has a text field or input to paste a challenge code
Entering a code starts a game with that seed, showing target score in the HUD
GameScene accepts a challengeCode parameter and uses its seed
CHALLENGE button in RootView is functional
Build succeeds
userStories.notes: RootView.swift already has a CHALLENGE button placeholder. GameMode enum already exists with .classic case - add .challenge(ChallengeCode).

userStories.title: Record tap timestamps during gameplay
userStories.description: Record the timestamp of every tap during a game run, relative to game start. Store as an array of TimeInterval. This data will be used for ghost replay.
acceptanceCriteria: GameScene records tap timestamps in an array during gameplay
Timestamps are relative to game start (first frame), not wall clock
Array is accessible after game over for encoding
Array resets on restart
Build succeeds
userStories.notes: Record in handleTap() using the currentTime from the update loop.

userStories.title: Ghost bird replay from tap timestamps
userStories.description: Add a ghost bird node that replays a recorded tap sequence. The ghost uses the same physics (gravity, impulse) but is rendered as a translucent outline. It runs independently of the player bird.
acceptanceCriteria: GameScene can accept an array of tap timestamps for ghost replay
Ghost bird is a semi-transparent node (e.g. 30% opacity, different color)
Ghost replays taps at the recorded timestamps using the same physics
Ghost does not collide with pipes (no physics contact)
Ghost is visible during challenge mode gameplay
Build succeeds
userStories.notes: Ghost bird needs its own physics body with contactTestBitMask = 0 and collisionBitMask = 0 so it passes through everything.

userStories.title: Integrate ghost with challenge codes
userStories.description: Extend the challenge code to include tap timestamps so the ghost duel is fully self-contained. When a challenge code is received, the ghost replays the challenger's run.
acceptanceCriteria: ChallengeCode includes tap timestamp data
Challenge code string is still shareable (may be longer but still text-based)
Receiving a challenge code shows the ghost of the original player
Ghost disappears if it dies (hits a pipe at the ghost's Y position)
Build succeeds
userStories.notes: The code will be longer with tap data. Consider compressing the timestamps (delta encoding + base64). Keep it under ~200 chars if possible.

userStories.title: Generate share card image
userStories.description: After a game over, generate a shareable image card with the score, best score, challenge code, and a CTA. Match the dark neo aesthetic.
acceptanceCriteria: ShareCard struct/class generates a UIImage
Card shows: score, best score, challenge code text, 'Can you beat me?' CTA
Dark background matching app theme
Image is suitable for sharing (roughly 1080x1920 or square)
File location: FlapFight/UI/ShareCard.swift
Build succeeds
userStories.notes: Use UIGraphicsImageRenderer to draw the card programmatically. Keep it simple - text on dark background with accent colors.

userStories.title: Share sheet integration
userStories.description: Add a share button that presents UIActivityViewController with the share card image and challenge code text.
acceptanceCriteria: Share button visible on death overlay or RootView
Tapping share opens iOS share sheet
Share sheet includes the generated card image and challenge code as text
Works correctly with Messages, Instagram, etc.
Build succeeds
userStories.notes: Use SwiftUI's ShareLink or wrap UIActivityViewController. The share button should appear after game over.
